records.text_en: Muhammad Abu al-Hasan related to us that Abu Hanifah reported from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God ﷻ be pleased with him, that he performed ablution washing his hands twice, rinsing his mouth twice, sniffing water into his nose twice, washing his face twice, washing his forearms twice—front and back—wiping his head twice, and washing his feet twice. Hammad said Once is sufficient if done thoroughly. Muhammad said: We adopt this practice.
records.text_ar: قَالَ مُحَمَّد أَبُو الْحَسن، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ الْأَسْوَدِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ «تَوَضَّأَ فَغَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ مَثْنَى، وَتَمَضْمَضَ مَثْنَى، وَاسْتَنْشَقَ مَثْنَى، وَغَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ مَثْنَى، وَغَسَلَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ مَثْنَى، مُقْبِلًا وَمُدْبِرًا، وَمَسَحَ رَأْسَهُ مَثْنَى، وَغَسَلَ رِجْلَيْهِ مَثْنَى» وَقَالَ حَمَّادٌ: الْوَاحِدَةُ تُجْزِئُ إِذَا اسُبِغَتْ ⦗ص: 2⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهَذَا نَأْخُذُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Wash the front of your ears with the face, and wipe the back of your ears with the head.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّد قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «اغْسِلْ مُقَدَّمَ ⦗ص: 3⦘ أُذُنَيْكَ مَعَ الْوَجْهِ، وَامْسَحْ مُؤَخَّرَ أُذُنَيْكَ مَعَ الرَّأْسِ» .

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah, ؓ, said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: The ears are part of the head. Muhammad, ؒ, said: We prefer to wipe the front and back of them with the head, and we adopt this.
records.text_ar: قَالَ مُحَمَّد: قَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ رضي الله عنه: بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلّى الله ⦗ص: 4⦘ عليه وسلم قَالَ: «الْأُذُنَانِ مِنَ الرَّأْسِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ رحمه الله: يُعْجِبُنَا أَنْ ⦗ص: 5⦘ نَمْسَحَ مُقَدَّمَهمَا، وُمُؤَخَّرَهمَا مَعَ الرَّأْسِ، وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah informed us, he said Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: Ablution is the key to prayer, the takbir makes it forbidden (to engage in other acts), and the taslim makes it permissible (to do so). No prayer is valid except with the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah), along with something else, and in every two rak'ahs, greet (by saying taslim). He meant: then testify. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and if one recites only the Mother of the Quran (al-Fatihah), he has done wrong, but it suffices him.
records.text_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي نَضْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلّى الله ⦗ص: 6⦘ عليه وسلم قَالَ «الْوُضُوءُ مِفْتَاحُ الصَّلَاةِ، وَالتَّكْبِيرُ تَحْرِيمُهَا، وَالتَّسْلِيمُ ⦗ص: 7⦘ تَحْلِيلُهَا، وَلَا تُجْزِئُ صَلَاةٌ إِلَّا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ، وَمَعَهَا ⦗ص: 8⦘ غَيْرُهَا، وَفِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، فَسَلِّمْ» يَعْنِي فَتَشَهَّدْ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَإِنْ قَرَأَ ⦗ص: 9⦘ بِأُمِّ الْقُرْآنِ وَحْدَهَا فَقَدْ أَسَاءَ وَتُجْزِيهِ

records.isnad_en: Abu Hanifah informed us, he said Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said:
records.matn_en: Ablution is the key to prayer, the takbir makes it forbidden (to engage in other acts), and the taslim makes it permissible (to do so). No prayer is valid except with the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah), along with something else, and in every two rak'ahs, greet (by saying taslim). He meant: then testify. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and if one recites only the Mother of the Quran (al-Fatihah), he has done wrong, but it suffices him.
records.boundary_review_note: The Prophet is the final named transmitter; the saying begins at the report verb.

records.text_en: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to us that Abu Hanifa informed him from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a cat drinking from a vessel. He said "It is one of the household; there is no harm in drinking what it leaves." I then asked him: "Can one perform ablution with what it leaves for prayer?" He replied: "God has made water permissible, neither commanding nor forbidding it."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifa said: "Something else is preferable to me over it, but if one performs ablution with it, it suffices." He also said: "Similarly, drinking something else is preferable to me, but if one drinks it, there is no harm in it." Muhammad said: "We adopt the opinion of Abu Hanifa."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "There is no good in the leftover water of a mule or donkey, and one does not perform ablution with the leftover water of a mule or donkey. However, one may perform ablution with the leftover water of a horse, a pony, a sheep, or a camel." Muhammad said: "This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abdillah ibn Abi al-Jahm narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Umar, ؓ, who said: I came to Iraq for the Battle of Jalula and saw Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, ؓ, wiping over his leather socks. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, from Hanzalah ibn Nubatah al-Ju'fi that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: "Wiping over the leather socks is permitted for the resident for a day and a night, and for the traveler for three days and their nights, if you put them on while in a state of purity." Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, ؓ, that he went out with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, on a journey. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, went away to relieve himself, then returned wearing a Roman cloak with tight sleeves. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, rolled them up due to the tightness of its sleeves. Al-Mughirah said: I began pouring water for him from a water skin I had with me, and he performed ablution as he would for prayer, wiping over his leather socks without removing them. Then he stepped forward and prayed.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلّى الله ⦗ص: 18⦘ عليه وسلم فِي سَفَرٍ، فَانْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَضَى حَاجَتَهُ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ وَعَلَيْهِ جُبَّةٌ رُومِيَّةٌ ضَيِّقَةُ الْكُمَّيْنِ، فَرَفَعَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ ضِيقِ ⦗ص: 19⦘ كُمَّيْهَا، قَالَ الْمُغِيرَةُ: فَجَعَلْتُ أَصُبُّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ مِنْ إِدَاوَةٍ مَعِي، فَتَوَضَّأَ وضُوءَهُ لِلصَّلَاةِ وَمَسَحَ عَلَى خُفَّيْهِ، وَلَمْ يَنْزِعْهُمَا، ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ فَصَلَّى "

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from someone who saw Jarir ibn Abdillah ؓone day performing ablution and wiping over his leather socks. A questioner asked him about that, so he said: I saw the Messenger of God ﷺdoing it, and I only accompanied him after Surah al-Ma'idah was revealed.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Harith, that Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar accompanied Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, on a journey. Three days and their nights passed, and he did not remove his leather socks.

records.isnad_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ،

records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim,
records.matn_en: that he would wipe over the leather socks. Muhammad said: And this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it.
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s reported practice begins the matn; Muhammad’s adoption note remains in it.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: If you are wearing leather socks and are in a state of ablution, then remove your leather socks, wash your feet. Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, and we adopt it.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «إِذَا كُنْتَ عَلَى مَسْحٍ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ، فَنَزَعْتَ خُفَّيْكَ فَاغْسِلْ قَدَمَيْكَ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s saying is in the isnad introduction; his instruction and Muhammad’s adoption note are matn.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: ‘Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, ؓ, that he said: “If I were brought a large bowl of bread and meat and ate from it until I was full, and a large cup of camel milk and drank from it until I was satiated, while I was in a state of ablution, I would not care if I did not touch water—do I perform ablution from what is wholesome?” Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it: there is no ablution required from what the fire has altered, for ablution is only from what exits, not from what enters.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَوْ أُتِيتُ بِجَفْنَةٍ مِنْ خُبْزٍ وَلَحْمٍ، فَأَكَلْتُ مِنْهَا حَتَّى أَشْبَعَ، وَبِعُسٍّ مِنْ لَبَنِ إِبِلٍ فَشَرِبْتُ مِنْهُ حَتَّى أَتَضَلَّعَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى وُضُوءٍ لَا أُبَالِي أَنْ لَا أَمَسَّ مَاءً، أَأَتَوَضَّأُ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ؟» قَالَ ⦗ص: 26⦘ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَهَذَا قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رضي الله عنه، وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ؛ لَا وُضُوءَ مِمَّا غَيَّرَتِ النَّارُ، وَإِنَّمَا الْوُضُوءُ مِمَّا خَرَجَ، وَلَيْسَ مِمَّا دَخَلَ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abdur-Rahman ibn Zadhan narrated to us, from Shurahbil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, entered my house, so I brought him some roasted meat, and he ate from it. Then he called for water, washed his hands, rinsed his mouth, and then prayed without performing a new ablution.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زَاذَانَ، عَنْ شُرَحْبِيلَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ دَخَلَ عَلَيَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 28⦘ بَيْتِي، فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِلَحْمٍ قَدْ شُوِيَ، فَطَعِمَ مِنْهُ، فَدَعَا بِمَاءٍ، فَغَسَلَ كَفَّيْهِ، وَمَضْمَضَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى، وَلَمْ يُحْدِثْ وُضُوءًا "

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Sa’id’s first-person account begins after the report verb.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah narrated to us, saying: Shaybah ibn Musawir narrated to us, saying: I was sitting with Adi ibn Artah when Al-Hasan al-Basri was asked, "Do I perform ablution from what the fire has touched?" He said, "Yes." Then Bakr ibn Abdillah al-Muzani said, "The Prophet, ﷺ, entered upon his aunt Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib, ؓ, and she plucked for him a cold shoulder of meat, so he ate from it and did not renew his ablution." Muhammad said: We adopt the opinion of Bakr ibn Abdillah al-Muzani, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا شَيْبَةُ بْنُ مُسَاوِرٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ قَاعِدًا عِنْدَ عَدِيِّ بْنِ أَرْطَأَةَ إِذْ سُئِلَ الْحَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيَّ: أَتَوَضَّأُ مِمَّا مَسَّتِ النَّارُ؟ فَقَالَ ⦗ص: 30⦘ : «نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ بَكْرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْمُزَنِيُّ: «دَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى عَمَّتِهِ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبٍ رضي الله عنها، فَنَتَفَتْ لَهُ مِنْ كَتِفٍ بَارِدَةٍ، فَطَعِمَ مِنْهَا وَلَمْ يُحْدِثْ وُضُوءًا» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِقَوْلِ بَكْرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْمُزَنِيِّ نَأْخُذُ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Abu Majid al-Hanafi, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: While we were sitting in the mosque with Ibn Mas'ud, a handful of food and a jug of water were brought to us from the Gate of the Elephant. Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, said: I see that you intend this for something. A man from the group said: Yes, O Abu Abd al-Rahman, there was a feast in the quarter, and this was set aside. He ate from it and drank from the water, then poured water over his hands, washed them, and wiped his face and forearms with the moisture on his hands. Then he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his state of purity. Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, and we adopt it. There is no harm in performing ablution in the mosque if it is free from filth.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who returns from a journey and his maternal aunt, paternal aunt, or a woman whom it is unlawful for him to marry kisses him. He said: "Wudu is not obligatory upon him if he kisses one whom it is unlawful for him to marry. However, if he kisses one whom it is lawful for him to marry, then wudu becomes obligatory upon him, and it is like the state of minor impurity." Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Ibrahim, but we do not adopt this view, nor do we consider wudu necessary for a kiss under any circumstance unless he emits pre-seminal fluid, in which case wudu is obligatory due to the pre-seminal fluid. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, regarding touching the penis, that he said: "It is all the same to me whether I touch it or the tip of my nose." Muhammad said: This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, was asked about ablution due to touching the penis. He said: "If it is impure, then cut it off," meaning there is no harm in it.

records.boundary_review_note: The report about Ibn Mas’ud begins matn after Ibrahim’s transmission.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, ؓ, passed by a man washing his penis and said: "What are you doing, woe to you! This (Quran 38:38) was not prescribed for you." Muhammad said: Washing it is more preferable to us after urinating, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Al-Haytham ibn Abi al-Haytham narrated to us from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, who said: "Four things are not defiled by anything: the body, the garment, the water, and the earth." Muhammad said: Our interpretation of this is that when filth touches them and they are washed, the filth is removed from them, so they do not retain any impurity. As for water, its meaning applies when it is abundant or flowing, as it does not retain filth.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا الْهَيْثَمُ بْنُ أَبِي الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما، قَالَ " أَرْبَعَةٌ لَا يُنَجِّسُهَا شَيْءٌ: الْجَسَدُ، وَالثَّوْبُ، وَالْمَاءُ، وَالْأَرْضُ " ⦗ص: 40⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَتَفْسِيرُ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَنَا أَنَّ ذَلِكَ إِذَا أَصَابَهُ الْقَذَرُ، فَغُسِلَ ذَهَبَ ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ، فَلَمْ يَحْمِلْ قَذَرًا، وَإِنَّمَا مَعْنَاهُ فِي الْمَاءِ إِذَا كَانَ كَثِيرًا أَوْ جَارِيًا أَنَّهُ لَا يَحْمِلُ خَبَثًا

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would put his head out of the mosque while he was in seclusion, and Aisha, ؓ, would wash it while she was menstruating. Muhammad said: We adopt this position and see no harm in it, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s report about the Messenger begins matn; the Prophet is a matn subject, not an additional transmitter in this route.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that while the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was walking, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, ؓ, came across him. The Prophet, ﷺ, leaned on him, but Hudhayfah withdrew his hand. The Prophet, ﷺ, asked, "What is the matter with you?" Hudhayfah replied, "O Messenger of God, I am in a state of major ritual impurity." The Prophet, ﷺ, said, "The believer is not impure." Muhammad said: We follow the hadith of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and see no harm in shaking hands with one in a state of major ritual impurity. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَمْشِي إِذْ عَرَضَ لَهُ حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ الْيَمَانٍ رضي الله عنهما ⦗ص: 42⦘ ، فَاعْتَمَدَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخَّرَ حُذَيْفَةُ يَدَهُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَا لَكَ؟» فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي جُنُبٌ، فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ لَيْسَ بِنَجَسٍ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِحَدِيثِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَأْخُذُ، لَا نَرَى بِمُصَافَحَةِ الْجُنُبِ بَأْسًا، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim that the resident patient among his family who is unable to use water due to smallpox or a wound that requires avoiding water is in the same position as the traveler who cannot find water; tayammum suffices for him. Muhammad said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ, and we adopt it.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ «أَنَّ الْمَرِيضَ الْمُقِيمَ فِي أَهْلِهِ الَّذِي لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ مِنَ الْجُدَرِيِّ وَالْجِرَاحَةِ الَّتِي يُتَّقَى عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءُ أَنَّهُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْمُسَافِرِ الَّذِي لَا يَجِدُ الْمَاءَ، يُجْزِيهِ التَّيَمُّمُ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَهَذَا قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رضي الله عنه، وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim regarding tayammum. He said: You place your palms on the clean earth, then wipe your face, then place them a second time, shake them off, and wipe your hands and arms up to the elbows. Muhammad said: We adopt this and hold the view, in addition to that, that one should shake off his hands each time before wiping his face and arms. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: When a man performs dry ablution (tayammum), he remains in a state of dry ablution as long as he does not find water or commit a ritual impurity. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim that he said: "It is more beloved to me that when one performs dry ablution (tayammum), one should reach up to the elbows." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and dry ablution is not valid unless one performs it up to the elbows. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: A man from the people of Basrah narrated to us from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he said: There is no harm in the urine of any animal with a paunch. Muhammad said: Abu Hanifah used to dislike it and would say: If it falls into the water for ablution, it invalidates the ablution, and if a large amount of it touches the garment, then he prays in it, he must repeat the prayer. Muhammad said: But I do not see any harm in it; it does not spoil water, ablution, or a garment.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا بَأْسَ بِبَوْلِ كُلِّ ذَاتِ كِرْشٍ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَكَانَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ يَكْرَهُهُ، وَكَانَ يَقُولُ: إِذَا وَقَعَ فِي وَضُوءٍ، أَفْسَدَ الْوُضُوءَ، وَإِنْ أَصَابَ الثَّوْبَ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ ثُمَّ صَلَّى فِيهِ أَعَادَ الصَّلَاةَ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَلَا أَرَى بِهِ بَأْسًا لَا يُفْسِدُ مَاءً وَلَا وُضُوءًا وَلَا ثَوْبًا
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: A man from the people of Basrah narrated to us from Al-Hasan Al-Basri
records.matn_en: that he said: There is no harm in the urine of any animal with a paunch. Muhammad said: Abu Hanifah used to dislike it and would say: If it falls into the water for ablution, it invalidates the ablution, and if a large amount of it touches the garment, then he prays in it, he must repeat the prayer. Muhammad said: But I do not see any harm in it; it does not spoil water, ablution, or a garment.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim regarding a man who urinates while standing and has dirhams with him containing writing, meaning the Quran. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim that the polytheists in the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, met the Muslims and said, "We see that your companion teaches you how to relieve yourselves, mocking you." The Muslims replied, "Yes." So they asked them, and the Muslims said, "He commanded us not to face the qiblah with our private parts, not to cleanse ourselves with our right hands, not to cleanse ourselves with bones or dung, and to cleanse ourselves with three stones." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and washing with water for cleansing is more beloved to us, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.raw_text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim that the polytheists in the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, met the Muslims and said, "We see that your companion teaches you how to relieve yourselves, mocking you." The Muslims replied, "Yes." So they asked them, and the Muslims said, "He commanded us not to face the qiblah with our private parts, not to cleanse ourselves with our right hands, not to cleanse ourselves with bones or dung, and to cleanse ourselves with three stones." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and washing with water for cleansing is more beloved to us, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a man who performs ablution and then wipes his face with his garment. He said: "There is no harm in it." Then he said: "Do you not see that if he were to bathe on a cold night, would he stand until it dries?" Muhammad said: We adopt this view and see no harm in it, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim regarding the man who trims his nails or cuts his hair, he said: "Water should pass over it." Muhammad said: I heard Abu Hanifah say: "Sometimes I trim my nails and cut my hair and do not let water pass over them until I pray." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abu Ali narrated to us, from Tammam, from Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said: Why do I see you entering upon me with yellowed teeth? Use the tooth-stick. Were it not that I would burden my nation, I would have commanded them to use the tooth-stick at every prayer. Muhammad said: The tooth-stick is, in our view, from the Sunnah; it should not be abandoned.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i narrated to us from al-Aswad ibn Yazid, from Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, ؓ, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, would be intimate with his wife at the beginning of the night, then sleep without having washed with water. If he awoke later in the night, he would return and perform ghusl. Muhammad said: We adopt this position. There is no harm if a man is intimate with his wife and then sleeps before performing ghusl or wudu. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the woman experiencing istihadah (non-menstrual bleeding): She should leave the Dhuhr prayer until the end of its time, then perform ghusl and pray Dhuhr, then pray Asr. Then she should wait until the time of Maghrib enters, leave the prayer until the end of its time, then perform ghusl and pray Maghrib and Isha until she is done. Muhammad said: We do not adopt this opinion. Instead, we follow the other hadith that she should perform wudu for each prayer time and pray within that time. According to us, she is only required to perform one ghusl until her days of bleeding pass. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Ayyub ibn Utbah, judge of al-Yamamah, reported to us from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan asked the Messenger of God, ﷺ, about the woman experiencing istihadah. He said: She should perform a full ritual bath when her menstrual days have passed, then perform ablution for each prayer and pray. Muhammad said: We adopt this hadith.

narrator_path.name_en: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
narrator_path.source_form: أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ

records.boundary_review_note: Umm Habibah is the source of the reported question; Muhammad’s concluding note is retained in matn.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When a woman menstruates during the time of a prayer, she is not required to make up that prayer. But if she becomes pure during the time of a prayer, then let her pray. Muhammad said: We adopt this position, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When a woman becomes in a state of major ritual impurity and then menstruates, she does not need to perform a ritual bath, for what affects her from menstruation is more severe than what affects her from major ritual impurity. Muhammad said: We adopt this position—she does not need to perform a ritual bath until she becomes pure from her menstruation, then she performs one ritual bath for both. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When a woman becomes pure during the time of a prayer but does not perform the ritual bath until the time for that prayer has passed—after having been occupied with her bath—then she is not required to make up that prayer. If the bleeding stops during a time when she cannot perform the ritual bath before the prayer’s time elapses, then she is not required to repeat that prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: "The woman in postpartum bleeding, if she has no fixed duration, remains seated for the duration of her womenfolk's days." Muhammad said: We do not adopt this, but rather she is considered in postpartum bleeding for up to forty days. If she exceeds that, she performs ghusl, performs wudu for every prayer time, and prays. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: "There is no harm in a mu’adhdhin calling the adhan while not in a state of wudu." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: I asked him about the *tathweeb* (calling to prayer a second time). records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Talhah ibn Musarrif narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: When the muezzin says, "Come to success," it is appropriate for the people to stand and form rows. When the muezzin says, "The prayer has begun," the imam should say the takbir. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ. If the imam waits until the muezzin finishes the iqamah and then says the takbir, there is no harm in that either; all of this is good.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim that a man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, asking about the times of prayer. He ordered him to attend the prayers with the Messenger of God, ﷺ. Then he ordered Bilal, ؓ, to hasten the prayers. The next day, he ordered him to delay all the prayers. Then he said: "Where is the one who asked about the time of prayer? The time is between these two." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and the Maghrib prayer and others are the same in this regard according to us, except that we dislike delaying it once the sun has set. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، يَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ الصَّلَاةِ، فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَحْضُرَ الصَّلَوَاتِ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِلَالًا رضي الله عنه أَنْ يُبَكِّرَ بِالصَّلَوَاتِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُ فِي الْيَوْمِ الثَّانِي، فَأَخَّرَ الصَّلَوَاتِ كُلَّهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ «أَيْنَ السَّائِلُ عَنْ وَقْتِ الصَّلَاةِ مَا بَيْنَ هَذَيْنِ وَقْتٌ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَالْمَغْرِبُ وَغَيْرُهَا عِنْدَنَا فِي هَذَا سَوَاءٌ إِلَّا أَنَّا نَكْرَهُ تَأْخِيرَهَا، إِذَا غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim
records.matn_en: that a man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, asking about the times of prayer. He ordered him to attend the prayers with the Messenger of God, ﷺ. Then he ordered Bilal, ؓ, to hasten the prayers. The next day, he ordered him to delay all the prayers. Then he said: "Where is the one who asked about the time of prayer? The time is between these two." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and the Maghrib prayer and others are the same in this regard according to us, except that we dislike delaying it once the sun has set. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: The report about the man and the Prophet begins matn; Muhammad’s position follows.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he said: "Delay the Zuhr prayer from the intense heat of Hell." Muhammad said: You delay the Zuhr prayer in the summer until it cools down, and you pray it in the winter when the sun has passed its zenith. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, looked at the sun when it had set and said, "This is when it has rubbed (against the horizon)."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I saw Ibrahim going out to the two Eids and he did not take a bath. Muhammad said: If you take a bath on Friday and the two Eids, it is better, but if you leave it, there is no harm.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Aban narrated to us from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: "Whoever takes a bath on Friday has done well, and whoever does not, then it is acceptable and good." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that some people from the people of Basrah came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, only to ask him about the opening of the prayer. Blessed is Your Name, and exalted is Your Majesty. There is no god but You." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Whoever does not say the takbir when beginning the prayer is not in a state of prayer. Muhammad said: We adopt this view, except if when he says the takbir for bowing, he says it while standing upright intending thereby to enter the prayer, then that suffices for him. records.display_text_en: Muḥammad said Abū Ḥanīfa reported to us from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, who said: “One who prayed beside ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and tried hard to hear his voice, told us that he heard nothing except that he heard him say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge’ (Ṭā Hā 20:114), repeating it several times. The man thought that he was reciting from Sūrat Ṭā Hā.” Muḥammad said: “This was during a daytime prayer. We see no harm in a person pausing at a passage of the Qur’an like this to supplicate for himself during a voluntary prayer; as for an obligatory prayer, he should not do so.”

records.matn_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا مَنْ صَلَّى إِلَى جَانِبِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه وَحَرَصَ عَلَى أَنْ يَسْمَعَ صَوْتَهُ فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَهُ يَقُولُ: {رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا} [طه: 114] يُرَدِّدُهَا مِرَارًا، فَظَنَّ الرَّجُلُ أَنَّهُ يَقْرَأُ فِي طَهْ " قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَهَذَا فِي صَلَاةِ النَّهَارِ فَلَا نَرَى بَأْسًا أَنْ يَقِفَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مِثْلِ هَذَا يَدْعُو لِنَفْسِهِ فِي التَّطَوُّعِ فَأَمَّا فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَلَا
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said:
records.matn_en: It was reported to us— —whoever prayed beside Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, and strove to hear his voice but did not hear anything except that he heard him saying, *"My Lord, increase me in knowledge"* (Ta-Ha: 114), repeating it several times. The man thought he was reciting in Surah Ta-Ha. : Muhammad said: This was during the daytime prayer, so we see no harm in a man pausing on something from the Quran like this, supplicating for himself in the voluntary prayer. As for the obligatory prayer, he should not do so.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: I said, "Should I say, 'In the name of God'?" He said, "Say, 'All greetings are for God.'" Muhammad said: We adopt this view. We do not see that anything should be added to the tashahhud or subtracted from it, not even a letter. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ قُلْتُ: أَقُولُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: قُلِ «التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ» ⦗ص: 145⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، لَا نَرَى أَنْ يُزَادَ فِي التَّشَهُّدِ وَلَا يُنْقَصَ مِنْهُ حَرْفٌ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: During the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, they would recite the tashahhud and say in their tashahhud, "Peace be upon God." One day, the Prophet, ﷺ, turned away and then faced them, saying, "Do not say, 'Peace be upon God,' for God is the source of peace. Rather, say: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.'" Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Yazid, from his father, who said: I prayed behind an imam who pronounced aloud "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "There are four things the Imam recites quietly: 'Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You,' seeking refuge from Satan, 'In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate,' and 'Amin.'" records.matn_ar: «اقْرَأْ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فِي الظُّهْرِ وَالْعَصْرِ، وَلَا تَقْرَأْ فِيمَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُقْرَأَ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّلَوَاتِ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he used to say: "Straighten your rows, align your shoulders, stand close together, or Satan will surely slip among you like small goats. Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon those who straighten the rows." Muhammad said: We adopt this view. It is not appropriate to leave a gap in the row until it is straightened. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim about the first row—does it have virtue over the second row? He said: It used to be said, “Do not stand in the row”—meaning the second—“until the first row is complete.” Muhammad said: We adopt this view. It is not proper, once the first row is complete, to crowd into it, for that causes harm. Standing in the second row is better than causing harm.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: The most versed in the Book of God leads the people in prayer. If they are equal in recitation, then the one who emigrated first. If they are equal in emigration, then the eldest in age. Muhammad said: We adopt this. It was said "the most versed in the Book of God" because at that time, the most versed in the Quran were the most knowledgeable in religion. If people in this time are like that, then let the most versed lead them. But if another is more knowledgeable in jurisprudence and more aware of the Sunnah of prayer, while his recitation is similar, then the more knowledgeable in jurisprudence and more aware of the Sunnah of prayer is more entitled to lead. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: "There is no harm in an Arab Bedouin, a slave, or a child born out of wedlock leading them in prayer if he recites the Quran." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, placed them behind him and prayed in front of them. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Al-Haytham ibn Abi al-Haytham narrated to us, raising it to the Prophet, ﷺ, that two men from the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, prayed Dhuhr in their homes, believing that the prayer had already been performed. They then came while the Prophet, ﷺ, was in prayer. They sat down and did not join. When the Prophet, ﷺ, finished, he called them, and they came with their joints trembling in fear that something had occurred regarding them. He said to them: "What prevented you from praying?" They said: "O Messenger of God, we thought the prayer had already been performed, so we prayed in our dwellings. Then we came and found you in prayer, so we thought it was not proper to pray again." He said: "If that is the case, then join the prayer, and consider the first one as the obligatory prayer and this one as voluntary." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ. The Fajr, Asr, and Maghrib prayers are not to be repeated.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Malik ibn Anas reported from Nafi‘ from Ibn ‘Umar, ؓ, who said: If you have prayed the dawn and sunset prayers, then caught up with them, do not repeat them beyond what you have already prayed. Muhammad said: As for the dawn and afternoon prayers, it is not appropriate to pray a voluntary prayer after them, due to the statement of the Messenger of God, ﷺ: No prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets, and no prayer after the dawn prayer until the sun rises. As for the sunset prayer, it is the witr of the day, and it is disliked to pray a voluntary prayer as witr. If a man enters with them as a volunteer, and the imam gives the salutation, he should stand, add a fourth rak‘ah to it, make the tashahhud, and give the salutation. All of this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us from al-Hasan al-Basri that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would pray voluntary prayers while sitting with his knees drawn up to his chest. Muhammad said: We adopt this view and see no harm in it. When he reached prostration, he would undo his sitting position. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar, ؓ, would perform the voluntary prayer while riding his mount, bowing wherever it faced him. But when it was the obligatory prayer or the Witr, he would dismount and pray. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding a man who joins a congregation in prayer without intending it, he said: "It is a voluntary prayer." Muhammad said: We adopt this view. It means that he had already prayed the prayer at home, then came to the people and joined them in their prayer, so his prayer with them is voluntary. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he used to lead them in prayer and stand to the left of the arch or to its right. Muhammad said: As for us, we see no harm in standing directly in line with the arch as long as he does not enter it when his standing place is outside of it and his prostration is within it. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said: When the imam gives the salutation (to end the prayer), the man should not turn away until the imam has turned away, unless the imam does not understand the affairs of the prayer. Muhammad said: We adopt this, because one does not know—perhaps the imam has to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness. If the imam is one who does not understand the affairs of the prayer, then there is no harm in turning away. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Alqamah ibn Marthad narrated to us from Ali, from Humran, who said: Whenever Ibn Umar ؓ was found narrating, Humran would be among the closest people to him in seating. He said: One day, Ibn Umar said to him, "O Humran, I see that you only cling to us to acquire some good." He replied, "Yes, O Abu Abdur-Rahman." Ibn Umar said, "Consider three things—two of which I forbid you from, and one which I command you to do." Humran asked, "What are they, O Abu Abdur-Rahman?" He said, "Do not die while you still have a debt unless it is a debt for which you leave behind sufficient payment. Do not ever deny any of your children, for on the Day of Resurrection, it will be proclaimed against you just as you proclaimed against them in this world—a just retribution, for your Lord does not wrong anyone. And observe the two rak'ahs of Fajr; do not abandon them, for they are among the most desirable acts."
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَلْقَمَةُ بْنُ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ⦗ص: 296⦘ ، عَنْ حُمْرَانَ، قَالَ مَا لُقِيَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما يُحَدِّثُ، إِلَّا وَحُمْرَانُ مِنْ أَقْرَبِ النَّاسِ مِنْهُ مَجْلِسًا. قَالَ: فَقَالَ لَهُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ: «يَا حُمْرَانُ إِنِّي لَأَرَاكَ ⦗ص: 297⦘ مَا لَزِمْتَنَا إِلَّا لِنَقْبِسَنَّكَ خَيْرًا» . قَالَ: أَجَلْ، يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ قَالَ: «انْظُرْ ثَلَاثًا، أَمَّا اثْنَتَانِ، فَأَنْهَاكَ عَنْهُمَا وَأَمَّا وَاحِدَةٌ، فَآمُرُكَ بِهَا» قَالَ: مَا هُنَّ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ؟ قَالَ: «لَا تَمُوتَنَّ، وَعَلَيْكَ دَيْنٌ إِلَّا دَيْنًا تَدَعُ لَهُ وَفَاءً، وَلَا تَنْتَفِيَنَّ مِنْ وَلَدٍ لَكَ أَبَدًا، فَإِنَّهُ يُسَمِّعُ بِكَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كَمَا سَمَّعْتَ بِهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا قِصَاصًا لَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا، وَانْظُرْ رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ، فَلَا تَدَعْهُمَا؛ فَإِنَّهُمَا مِنَ الرَّغَائِبِ»

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim about the mu’adhdhins who call the adhan above the mosque and then pray above the mosque. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I saw Ibrahim praying in a place where there was much sand and thick dust, and he would wipe his face before turning away. Muhammad said: We see no harm in wiping the face before the tashahhud and taslim, for leaving it may harm the one praying and may distract him from his prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "A man's prayer while sitting is like half of a man's prayer while standing." And this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، قَالَ «صَلَاةُ الرَّجُلِ قَاعِدًا عَلَى مِثْلِ نِصْفِ صَلَاةِ الرَّجُلِ قَائِمًا» وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: It is not sufficient for a man to place a whip or a reed in front of him unless he sets it up properly. Muhammad said: Setting it up properly is preferable to us, but if he does not do so, his prayer is still valid. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ لَا يُجْزِئُ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَعْرِضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ سَوْطًا وَلَا قَصَبَةً حَتَّى يَنْصِبَهُ نَصْبًا " ⦗ص: 315⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: النَّصْبُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا فَإِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ أَجْزَأَتْهُ صَلَاتُهُ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Abdullah ibn Umar, ؓ, would, when he prostrated and prolonged it, rest his elbows on his thighs. Muhammad said: We see no harm in that, and that is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Ibrahim that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would place one of his hands over the other in prayer, humbling himself before God ﷻ. Muhammad said: And he would place the palm of his right hand over the wrist of his left beneath the navel, so that the wrist would be in the middle of the palm.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَعْتَمِدُ بِإِحْدَى يَدَيْهِ عَلَى الْأُخْرَى فِي الصَّلَاةِ، يَتَوَاضَعُ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى " ⦗ص: 321⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَيَضَعُ بَطْنَ كَفِّهِ الْأَيْمَنِ عَلَى رُسْغِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ تَحْتَ السُّرَّةِ فَيَكُونُ الرُّسْغُ فِي وَسَطِ الْكَفِّ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Al-Rabi' ibn Subayh reported to us from Abu Ma'shar from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he used to place his right hand over his left below the navel. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Zubayd al-Yami narrated to us, from Dhirr al-Hamdani, from Sa'id, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, ؓ, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, used to recite in the Witr prayer in the first rak'ah: *Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High*, and in the second: *Say: O you who disbelieve*—meaning *Say: O you disbelievers*, as it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ—and in the third: *Say: He is God, the One*. Muhammad said: If you recite this, it is good in our view. Whatever you recite from the Quran in Witr along with the Opening of the Book is also good, as long as you recite at least three verses or more along with the Opening of the Book. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا زُبَيْدٌ الْيَامِيُّ ⦗ص: 327⦘ ، عَنْ ذَرٍّ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبْزَى رضي الله عنه قَالَ «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ فِي الْوِتْرِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى بِ سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى، وَفِي الثَّانِيَةِ» قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا «يَعْنِي قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ وَهِيَ هَكَذَا فِي قِرَاءَةِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، وَفِي الثَّالِثَةِ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ» ⦗ص: 329⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: إِنْ قَرَأْتَ بِهَذَا فَهُوَ عِنْدَنَا حَسَنٌ وَمَا قَرَأْتَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فِي الْوِتْرِ مَعَ فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ فَهُوَ أَيْضًا حَسَنٌ إِذَا قَرَأْتَ مَعَ فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ بِثَلَاثِ آيَاتٍ فَصَاعِدًا وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he said: I would not like to have abandoned the Witr prayer for three camels, even if I owned red camels. Muhammad said: We adopt this. The Witr prayer consists of three rak'ahs that are not separated by a taslim, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said: If one reaches the morning without having performed Witr, then there is no Witr. Muhammad said: We do not adopt this view. One should perform Witr in any case, except at a time when prayer is disliked—when the sun rises until it becomes bright, or when it is at its zenith until it declines, or when it reddens until it sets. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding "the man who prays the obligatory prayer in the mosque, then the muezzin calls the iqamah while he is in a rak'ah." He said: He completes another rak'ah to it, then joins the congregation's prayer with a takbir. When the imam prays two rak'ahs and sits for the tashahhud, the man offers salam to his right and left to himself, then stands, says takbir, and prays with the imam the remaining part of his prayer as voluntary. He does not join the congregation's prayer except in an even number of his prayer. Amir al-Sha'bi said: He adds another rak'ah to it and departs, then joins the congregation. Muhammad said: The statement of al-Sha'bi is more beloved to us, and it is the statement of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When one enters the mosque and the people are bowing, let him bow without rushing. Muhammad said: We do not adopt this view; rather, he should walk calmly until he reaches the row and prays what he catches and makes up what he missed.

records.text_en: Muhammad from Mubarak ibn Fadalah from al-Hasan al-Basri from Abu Bakrah, ؓ, that he bowed in prayer behind the row, then walked until he reached the row. This was mentioned to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and he said "May God increase your eagerness, but do not do it again." Muhammad said: We adopt this view; we consider it sufficient, but we do not like that one should do it. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، عَنْ مُبَارَكِ بْنِ فَضَالَةَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ رَكَعَ دُونَ الصَّفِّ ثُمَّ مَشَى حَتَّى وَصَلَ الصَّفَّ، فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ «زَادَكَ اللَّهُ حِرْصًا وَلَا تَعُدْ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، نَرَى ذَلِكَ مُجْزِئًا، وَلَا يُعْجِبُنَا أَنْ يَفْعَلَ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ ⦗ص: 349⦘ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba reported from Qatada from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, and al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Khilas ibn 'Amr that they said: "Whoever catches one rak'ah of the Friday prayer should add another to it, and whoever finds them sitting should pray four." This was also reported to us from 'Alqama ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, and this is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri, Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl, and we adopt this view.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Masruq and Jundub joined the Imam in the Maghrib prayer and caught one rak'ah with him but missed two. They prayed one rak'ah with him, then stood to make up what they had missed. Masruq sat in the first rak'ah he made up, while Jundub stood in the first and sat in the second. When they finished, each turned to the other, then they raced to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, and told him the story. He said: "Both of you have done well, but I prefer to pray as Masruq prayed." Muhammad said: We follow the opinion of Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ—he sits in the two rak'ahs he missed. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ مَسْرُوقًا، وَجُنْدُبًا، دَخَلَا فِي صَلَاةِ الْإِمَامِ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فَأَدْرَكَا مَعَهُ رَكْعَةً وَسُبِقَا بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ فَصَلَّيَا مَعَهُ رَكْعَةً، ثُمَّ قَامَا يَقْضِيَانِ، فَأَمَّا مَسْرُوقٌ فَجَلَسَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى الَّتِي قَضَى، وَأَمَّا جُنْدُبٌ، فَقَامَ فِي الْأُولَى، وَجَلَسَ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَا، أَقْبَلَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا تَسَاوَقَا إِلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه ⦗ص: 353⦘ فَقَصَّا عَلَيْهِ الْقِصَّةَ، فَقَالَ «كِلَاكُمَا قَدْ أَحْسَنَ، وَأَنْ أُصَلِّيَ كَمَا صَلَّى مَسْرُوقٌ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِقَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه نَأْخُذُ. يَجْلِسُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اللَّتَيْنِ فَاتَتَاهُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding "a man whom the Imam has preceded in some part of his prayer—does he recite the tashahhud every time the Imam sits?" He said: Yes. He asked: Does he return the salutation when the Imam gives salam? He said: When he finishes his prayer, he returns the salutation. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "If the prayer of the imam becomes invalid, the prayer of those behind him also becomes invalid." Muhammad said: We adopt this position. If a man leads his companions in prayer while in a state of major ritual impurity, or without ablution, or if his prayer becomes invalid for any reason, the prayer of those behind him also becomes invalid.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Makki reported to us from Amr ibn Dinar that Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, said regarding "a man who leads people in prayer while in a state of major ritual impurity: He must repeat his prayer, and they must repeat theirs."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak reported to us from Abdullah ibn Awn, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "It is more beloved to me that they repeat." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the statement of Abu Hanifa, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: If a woman prays beside a man and they are in the same prayer, his prayer is invalidated. Muhammad said: We adopt this position, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Aisha, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, would pray while she was sleeping beside him, and he had a garment with one side of it over her. Muhammad said: We adopt this practice and see no harm in it. Likewise, if she were to pray beside him in a prayer other than his, it would not be objectionable. The prayer is only invalidated if she prays beside him while both are in the same prayer, either following him or both following someone else. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim about "a man praying in the eastern side of the mosque and a woman in the western side." He disapproved of that unless there was something between him and her the size of the rear part of a saddle. Muhammad said: We adopt this view when they are in the same prayer, praying behind one imam.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ «الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي جَانِبِ الْمَسْجِدِ الشَّرْقِيِّ، وَالْمَرْأَةِ فِي الْغَرْبِيِّ، فَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا شَيْءٌ قَدْرَ مُؤَخِّرَةِ الرَّحْلِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، إِذَا كَانَا فِي صَلَاةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ يُصَلِّيَانِ مَعَ إِمَامٍ وَاحِدٍ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding the man who suffers a nosebleed during prayer or experiences an impurity. If he spoke, he must restart the prayer. Muhammad said: We adopt this position regarding speech, but restarting the prayer is preferable, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: If the blood is the size of a dirham, or urine or other [impurities], then repeat your prayer. records.matn_ar: لَا صَلَاةَ بَعْدَ الْغَدَاةِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ، وَلَا صَلَاةَ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ حَتَّى تَغْرُبَ ، وَلَا يُصَامُ هَذَانِ الْيَوْمَانِ: الْفِطْرُ وَالْأَضْحَى، وَلَا تُشَدُّ الرِّحَالُ إِلَّا إِلَى ثَلَاثَةِ مَسَاجِدَ: الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ، وَمَسْجِدِي وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى، وَلَا تُسَافِرُ الْمَرْأَةُ إِلَّا مَعَ ذِي مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهَا " قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهَذَا كُلِّهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَلَا يَنْبَغِي لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تُسَافِرَ إِلَّا مَعَ زَوْجِهَا أَوْ مَعَ ذِي مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهَا. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us from Qaza'ah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said:
records.matn_en: "There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and no prayer after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets. These two days are not to be fasted: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. Journeys should not be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, my mosque, and the Farthest Mosque. A woman should not travel except with a *mahram* from among her relatives." Muhammad said: We adhere to all of this, and it is not proper for a woman to travel except with her husband or with a *mahram* from among her relatives. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: The Prophetic statement begins matn; Muhammad’s application follows.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim that he "disapproved of cracking one's fingers during prayer, or letting one's cloak fall from the shoulders, or placing one's hand on the hip, or burying large pebbles, or squatting on the heels, or fidgeting with one's beard." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, led his companions in the Maghrib prayer but did not recite anything in any of its rak'ahs until he finished. His companions said to him, "What prevented you from reciting, O Commander of the Faithful?" He replied, "Did I not do so? I was preparing a caravan to Syria that evening and kept loading it bit by bit until it reached Syria." He repeated this, and his companions also repeated their question. Muhammad said: We adopt this position, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us from Abu Gadiyah that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, used to punish people for praying after Asr. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "I would not consider a man's prayer when the sun reddens worth two pennies." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: If the blood on your body or on your garment is the size of a dirham, repeat your prayer. If it is less than that, proceed with your prayer. Muhammad said: Blood on the garment and on the body are the same—if it is more than the size of a large dirham (mithqal), repeat the prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, from Abu Zur‘ah ibn ‘Amr ibn Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, regarding the man who finds moisture at the tip of his penis while he is in prayer. records.boundary_review_note: The report from Abu Hurayrah begins matn and includes a second exchange in which Hammad asks Ibrahim what he does.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, who said: When you find something of wetness, sprinkle it and the area of your garment around it with water, then say, "It is from the water." Hammad said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Sprinkle it with water, then if you find it, say, "It is from the water." Muhammad said: We adopt this position if that frequently happens to a person. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: There is no harm in a man covering his head during prayer as long as he does not cover his mouth, and it is disliked for him to cover his mouth. Muhammad said: We adopt this position, and we also dislike covering the nose, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a man who prays the Asr prayer and then remembers while praying that he had not prayed the Zuhr prayer. He said: "This prayer of his is invalid. He must start with Zuhr, then pray Asr." Muhammad said: We adopt this position, except in one case: if he fears missing the Asr prayer, and if he begins with Zuhr, he should continue with Asr, then pray Zuhr after the sun has set. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Mansur ibn Zadhan narrated to us from al-Hasan al-Basri, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said: While he was in prayer, a blind man approached from the direction of the qiblah intending to pray, and the people were in the Fajr prayer. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a man who laughs loudly during prayer. He said: "He must renew his ablution and his prayer, and seek forgiveness from his Lord, for it is the most severe of ritual impurities." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: I asked him about sleeping before the final evening prayer, and he said: "For me to pray it alone is more beloved to me than to sleep before it and then pray it in congregation." Muhammad said: We dislike sleeping before the 'Isha prayer, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, rested one night and said, "Who will guard us tonight?" A young man from the Ansar said, "I will, O Messenger of God, I will guard you." So he guarded them until, when it was near dawn, sleep overcame him, and they did not wake up until the sun had risen hot. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, then stood, performed ablution, and his companions did the same. He ordered the muezzin to call the adhan, then he prayed two rak'ahs. Then the iqamah was called, and he led his companions in the Fajr prayer, reciting aloud as he would at its proper time. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, regarding the one who loses consciousness for a day and a night: "He must make up [the missed prayers]." Muhammad said: We adopt this view until the loss of consciousness lasts longer than that. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding "a man who doubts in the prostration, or the testimony (Tashahhud), or something similar in his prayer—so long as it is not a complete unit (rak‘ah)—that he should perform what he doubts about from that, and also prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness for it, for they rectify, by God’s permission, whatever preceded them of forgetfulness. It was said: They are the ones that humiliate Satan. And he said: To prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness for that, in what has not become obligatory upon me, is more beloved to me than to leave them." Muhammad said: We adopt this position. If one is frequently afflicted by such doubts, he should proceed according to the stronger of his opinions and prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding one who forgets the obligatory prayer and does not know whether he prayed four or three rak'ahs. He said: "If it is the first time he forgets, he should repeat the prayer. If he frequently forgets, he should strive to determine what is correct. If his stronger assumption is that he completed the prayer, he should perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness. If his stronger assumption is that he prayed three, he should add one more and then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When two matters perplex you, assume that the one closer to the truth is the more lenient of the two.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: When the imam makes a mistake and prostrates the two prostrations of forgetfulness, prostrate with him. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When you finish your prayer and then doubt arises regarding ablution, prayer, or recitation, do not pay attention to it. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "The greeting is returned and the sneezer is blessed while the Imam is delivering the Friday sermon." Muhammad said: We do not adopt this, but rather we follow the opinion of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, may God ﷻ have mercy on him.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Sufyan ibn Uyaynah reported to us from Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, who said: I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, "A man sneezed while the Imam was delivering the sermon, and another man said *yarhamuk God* (may God have mercy on you) to him." He said, "Tell him not to do it again." Muhammad said: We adopt this position. The sermon holds the same status as prayer; one should not say *yarhamuk God* to a sneezer during it, nor return the greeting of peace. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ ⦗ص: 470⦘ أَبِي هِنْدٍ، قَالَ قُلْتُ لِسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ: إِنَّ فُلَانًا عَطَسَ، وَالْإِمَامُ يَخْطُبُ فَشَمَّتَهُ فُلَانٌ، قَالَ: «مُرْهُ فَلَا يَعُودَنَّ» ⦗ص: 471⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهَذَا نَأْخُذُ. الْخُطْبَةُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الصَّلَاةِ لَا يُشَمَّتُ فِيهَا الْعَاطِسُ ⦗ص: 472⦘ ، وَلَا يُرَدُّ فِيهَا السَّلَامُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the man who enters upon his companion while he is praying and greets him with peace: Does he not say in his tashahhud, "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God"? So he has already returned the greeting to him. Muhammad said: We adopt this view. However, we do not approve of returning the greeting while he is praying, nor do we approve of a man greeting him with peace while he is praying. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

Whoever leads a people in prayer should shorten it, for among them are the sick, the elderly, and those with needs." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is necessary to complete the bowing and prostration. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: Anonymous Companion is preserved as transmitted; the Prophet is the reported speaker in matn, not an isnad link.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Maymun ibn Siyah narrated to me from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: A man asked him, "Should I recite five hundred verses in one rak'ah?" Al-Hasan was astonished and said, "Glory be to God! Who can endure this?" The man replied, "I can endure it." Al-Hasan said, "The prayer most beloved to God is the length of devotion." Muhammad said: Prolonging the standing in voluntary prayer is more beloved to us than frequent bowing and prostration. All of this is good, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مَيْمُونُ بْنُ سِيَاهٍ ⦗ص: 484⦘ ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ، قَالَ سَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ: أَقْرَأُ خَمْسَمِائَةِ آيَةٍ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ، قَالَ: فَتَعَجَّبَ، وَقَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، مَنْ يُطِيقُ هَذَا؟ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ: أَنَا أُطِيقُ هَذَا، قَالَ: إِنَّ أَحَبَّ الصَّلَاةِ إِلَى اللَّهِ طُولُ الْقُنُوتِ " ⦗ص: 485⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: طُولُ الْقِيَامِ فِي صَلَاةِ التَّطَوُّعِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الرُّكُوعِ وَالسُّجُودِ ⦗ص: 487⦘ . وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ حَسَنٌ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah narrated to us from Hammad from Ibrahim that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, led his companions in the Fajr prayer. In the first rak'ah, he recited "Say: O disbelievers," and in the second, "For the accustomed security of the Quraysh." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and we consider it sufficient, but we prefer that when the imam leads the Fajr prayer as a resident, he should prolong the recitation, reciting in each rak'ah a surah of twenty verses or more besides the Opening of the Book, and he should make the first rak'ah longer than the second. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَمَّ أَصْحَابَهُ فِي صَلَاةِ الصُّبْحِ، فَقَرَأَ بِهِمْ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى بِـ قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ وَفِي الثَّانِيَةِ بِ لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَنَرَاهُ مُجْزِئًا وَلَكِنَّا نَسْتَحِبُّ لِلْإِمَامِ إِذَا صَلَّى ⦗ص: 488⦘ الصُّبْحَ، وَهُوَ مُقِيمٌ أَنْ يُطِيلَ فِيهَا الْقِرَاءَةَ، أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ بِسُورَةٍ تَكُونُ عِشْرِينَ آيَةً فَصَاعِدًا سِوَى فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَيُطِيلُ الْأُولَى عَلَى الثَّانِيَةِ، وَهُو قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Musa ibn Muslim narrated to us from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Umar, ؓ, who said: When you are traveling and intend to stay for fifteen days, then complete the prayer. But if you do not know when you will depart, then shorten it. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.display_text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، قَالَ «إِذَا كُنْتَ مُسَافِرًا، فَوَطَّنْتَ نَفْسَكَ عَلَى إِقَامَةِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا، فَأَتْمِمِ الصَّلَاةَ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَا تَدْرِي مَتَى تَظْعَنُ فَأَقْصِرْ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he led the people in Mecca in the Zuhr prayer with two rak'ahs, then turned to them and said: "O people of Mecca, we are travelers, so whoever is a resident should complete his prayer." The residents then completed their prayer. Muhammad said: We adopt this position—when a resident joins the prayer of a traveler and the traveler finishes his prayer, the resident stands and completes his prayer. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ ⦗ص: 494⦘ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ صَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ بِمَكَّةَ الظُّهْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ، فَقَالَ يَا أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ، إِنَّا قَوْمٌ سَفْرٌ، فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَلَدِ، فَلْيُكْمِلْ. فَأَكْمَلَ أَهْلُ الْبَلَدِ " ⦗ص: 495⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، إِذَا دَخَلَ الْمُقِيمُ فِي صَلَاةِ الْمُسَافِرِ فَقَضَى الْمُسَافِرُ صَلَاتَهُ، قَامَ الْمُقِيمُ، فَأَتَمَّ صَلَاتَهُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: When a traveler joins the prayer of a resident, he must complete it. Muhammad said: We adopt this view—if a traveler joins a resident, he must perform the resident’s prayer of four rak’ahs. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: "Do not let your gathering here deceive you—this is from your prayer. A man may be absent from his estate, so he shortens his prayer and says, 'I am a traveler.'" Muhammad said: We adopt this view. If one is on a journey of less than three days and their nights, he completes the prayer. If he is on a journey of three days and their nights or more, and he has no family there, nor has he settled himself for a stay of fifteen days, then let him shorten the prayer. If he has settled himself for a stay of fifteen days, he completes the prayer as long as he remains at his estate. When he departs, returning to his family, he shortens the prayer. A journey of three days and their nights is measured by the moderate pace of camels and the walking of feet, and this is the view of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ " لَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ مَحْشَرُكُمْ، هَذَا مِنْ صَلَاتِكُمْ، يَغِيبُ الرَّجُلُ ⦗ص: 500⦘ عَنْ ضَيْعَتِهِ، فَيَقْصُرُ، وَيَقُولُ: أَنَا مُسَافِرٌ " قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، إِذَا كَانَ عَلَى مَسِيرَةٍ أَقَلَّ مِنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيهَا أَتَمَّ الصَّلَاةَ، فَإِذَا كَانَ عَلَى مَسِيرَةِ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيهَا فَصَاعِدًا، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ بِهَا أَهْلٌ، وَلَمْ يُوَطِّنْ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى إِقَامَةِ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ، فَلْيُقْصِرِ الصَّلَاةَ، فَإِذَا وَطَّنَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى إِقَامَةِ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ، أَتَمَّ الصَّلَاةَ، مَا دَامَ فِي ضَيْعَتِهِ، فَإِذَا خَرَجَ رَاجِعًا إِلَى أَهْلِهِ، قَصَرَ الصَّلَاةَ. وَمَسِيرَةُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيهَا بِالْقَصْدِ بِسَيْرِ الْإِبِلِ، وَمَشْيِ الْأَقْدَامِ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.raw_text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: "Do not let your gathering here deceive you—this is from your prayer. A man may be absent from his estate, so he shortens his prayer and says, 'I am a traveler.'" Muhammad said: We adopt this view. If one is on a journey of less than three days and their nights, he completes the prayer. If he is on a journey of three days and their nights or more, and he has no family there, nor has he settled himself for a stay of fifteen days, then let him shorten the prayer. If he has settled himself for a stay of fifteen days, he completes the prayer as long as he remains at his estate. When he departs, returning to his family, he shortens the prayer. A journey of three days and their nights is measured by the moderate pace of camels and the walking of feet, and this is the view of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Sa'id ibn 'Ubayd al-Ta'i reported from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Walibi, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, ؓ, "How far may the prayer be shortened?" He replied, "Do you know al-Suwayda'?" I said, "No, but I have heard of it." He said, "It is three nights' journey for a traveler. When we set out for it, we shorten the prayer." Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: When a resident joins the prayer of a traveler, he should pray two rak'ahs with him, then stand and complete his prayer. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.display_text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «إِذَا دَخَلَ الْمُقِيمُ فِي صَلَاةِ الْمُسَافِرِ، فَلْيُصَلِّ مَعَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ لِيَقُمْ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلَاتَهُ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.matn_ar: إِذَا دَخَلَ الْمُقِيمُ فِي صَلَاةِ الْمُسَافِرِ، فَلْيُصَلِّ مَعَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ لِيَقُمْ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلَاتَهُ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.boundary_review_note: Muhammad’s school commentary follows the transmitted ruling.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding the Fear Prayer: When the Imam prays with his companions, let one group stand with the Imam while another group faces the enemy. The Imam shall lead the group with him in one rak'ah, then that group which prayed with the Imam shall depart without speaking until they stand in the place of their companions. The other group shall come and pray the remaining rak'ah with the Imam, then depart without speaking until they stand in the place of their companions. The first group shall then return to pray one rak'ah by themselves, then depart to stand in the place of their companions. The second group shall come to complete the rak'ah that remained for them by themselves. Muhammad said: Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman reported to us from Abdullah ibn Abbas, ؓ, the same as that. Muhammad said: We adopt all of this. As for the first group, they shall complete their rak'ah without recitation because they caught the beginning of the prayer with the Imam, so the Imam’s recitation suffices for them. As for the second group, they shall complete their rak'ah with recitation because it was missed with the Imam. All of this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Jawwab al-Taymi reported to us from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, ؓ, that a man came to him and said: I fear hypocrisy for myself. Abu Musa said to him: Have you ever prayed where no one sees you except God? He said: Yes. Abu Musa said: The hypocrite does not pray where no one sees him except God, the Mighty and Exalted.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا جَوَّابٌ التَّيْمِيُّ، عَنْ ⦗ص: 519⦘ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رضي الله عنه أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَاهُ، فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَتَخَوَّفُ عَلَى نَفْسِي النِّفَاقَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو مُوسَى: «أَمَا صَلَّيْتَ قَطُّ حَيْثُ لَا يَرَاكَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ» قَالَ: بَلَى، قَالَ: «فَإِنَّ الْمُنَافِقَ لَا يُصَلِّي حَيْثُ لَا يَرَاهُ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ عز وجل»

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: When a man sneezes and says, "All praise is due to God," you should say, "May God have mercy on us and you." And the one who sneezed should say, "May God forgive us and you."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Ghaylan and Ayyub ibn ‘Aidh al-Ta’i narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: Four are not obliged to attend Friday prayer: the woman, the slave, the traveler, and the sick. Abu Hanifah said: If they do attend, it suffices for them. Muhammad said: We adopt this position.
