records.text_en: Abu Hanifah reported from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that a man asked him about the sermon on Friday. He said Do you not recite Surah al-Jumu'ah? The man replied: Yes, but I do not know how it is. He said: *"But when they saw a transaction or an amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing."* So the sermon on Friday is delivered while standing. Muhammad said: We adopt this, except that it consists of two sermons with a brief sitting in between, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّ رَجُلًا سَأَلَهُ عَنِ الْخُطْبَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، فَقَالَ «أَمَا تَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ؟» قَالَ: بَلَى وَلَكِنِّي لَا أَدْرِي كَيْفَ هِيَ؟ قَالَ: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْا ⦗ص: 532⦘ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَائِمًا} [الجمعة: 11] «فَالْخُطْبَةُ قَائِمًا يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ» ⦗ص: 534⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، إِلَّا أَنَّهَا خُطْبَتَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا جِلْسَةٌ خَفِيفَةٌ وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: I asked Ibrahim about a man who goes out to the prayer ground and finds that the Imam has already finished—should he pray? He said: He does not have to pray, but if he wishes, he may. I said: If he does not go out to the prayer ground, should he pray at home as the Imam prayed? He said: No. Muhammad said: We adopt this position—the Eid prayer is only with the Imam, so if you miss it with the Imam, there is no prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.matn_en: I asked Ibrahim about a man who goes out to the prayer ground and finds that the Imam has already finished—should he pray? He said: He does not have to pray, but if he wishes, he may. I said: If he does not go out to the prayer ground, should he pray at home as the Imam prayed? He said: No. Muhammad said: We adopt this position—the Eid prayer is only with the Imam, so if you miss it with the Imam, there is no prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: Hammad’s first-person question and Ibrahim’s replies form matn.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he was sitting in the mosque of Kufah with Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, ؓ. Al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt—who was the governor of Kufah at that time—came to them and said: "Tomorrow is your Eid, so what should I do?" They said: "Tell him, O Abu Abd al-Rahman, what he should do." So Abdullah ibn Mas'ud instructed him to pray without a call to prayer or an announcement, to say five takbirs in the first rak'ah and four in the second, to recite the two recitations consecutively, and to deliver the sermon after the prayer while on his mount. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and there is no harm in delivering the sermon while standing even if not on a mount, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad reported: Abu Hanifah informed us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said The prayer during the two Eids used to be before the sermon. Then the Imam would stand on his mount after the prayer and supplicate and pray without a call to prayer or an announcement.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq, from Umm Atiyyah, ؓ, who said: "Women were permitted to go out for the two Eids: Fitr and Adha." Muhammad said: We do not approve of their going out for that except for the very old woman. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.isnad_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ بْنِ أَبِي الْمُخَارِقِ ، عَنْ أُمِّ عَطِيَّةَ، رضي الله عنها، قَالَتْ "
records.matn_ar: كَانَ يُرَخَّصُ لِلنِّسَاءِ فِي الْخُرُوجِ فِي الْعِيدَيْنِ: الْفِطْرِ وَالْأَضْحَى " قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: لَا يُعْجِبُنَا خُرُوجُهُنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ إِلَّا الْعَجُوزَ الْكَبِيرَةَ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq, from Umm Atiyyah, ؓ, who said: "
records.matn_en: Women were permitted to go out for the two Eids: Fitr and Adha." Muhammad said: We do not approve of their going out for that except for the very old woman. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: Umm Atiyyah’s statement ends before Muhammad’s legal assessment.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a group who testified that they had seen the crescent of Shawwal. Hammad said: I asked Ibrahim about that, and he said: "If they come at the beginning of the day, let them break their fast and go out. If they come at the end of the day, let them neither go out nor break their fast until the next day." Muhammad said: We adopt this view, except in one aspect: they break their fast and go out the next day if they come in the evening. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي قَوْمٍ شَهِدُوا أَنَّهُمْ رَأَوْا هِلَالَ شَوَّالٍ فَقَالَ حَمَّادٌ: سَأَلْتُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ: «إِنْ جَاءُوا صَدْرَ النَّهَارِ فَلْيُفْطِرُوا وَلْيَخْرُجُوا، وَإِنْ جَاءُوا آخِرَ النَّهَارِ، فَلَا يَخْرُجُوا وَلَا يُفْطِرُوا حَتَّى الْغَدِ» ⦗ص: 553⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، إِلَّا فِي خَصْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، يُفْطِرُونَ وَيَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْغَدِ إِذَا جَاءُوا مِنَ الْعَشِيِّ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he would say the takbir from the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah until the Asr prayer on the last of the Days of Tashriq. Muhammad said: We adopt this, though Abu Hanifah did not. Instead, he followed the opinion of Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who would say the takbir from the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah until the Asr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice, saying the takbir in the Asr prayer, then stopping.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he "did not prostrate in *Sad*." And from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he "did not prostrate in it." Muhammad said: But we consider prostration in it to be recommended, and we follow the hadith reported from the Messenger of God, ﷺ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Umar ibn Dhar al-Hamdani reported to us from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said regarding the prostration in *Sad*: "David prostrated in it as repentance, while we prostrate in it as gratitude." This is the saying of Surah *Sad*: 24, according to Abu Hanifa, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that "the qunut in the witr prayer is obligatory during the month of Ramadan and at other times before bowing. When you intend to perform qunut, say takbir, and when you intend to bow, say takbir again." Muhammad said: We adopt this. He raises his hands in the first takbir before the qunut as he raises them at the beginning of the prayer, then places them down and supplicates. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, "did not perform the qunut supplication, nor did any of his companions, until he departed this world—meaning in the Fajr prayer."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Al-Salt ibn Bahram narrated to us from Abu al-Sha'tha’ from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he said: The most accurate report we have received about your imam is that he stands in prayer, does not recite the Quran, and does not bow. Muhammad said: Ibn Umar, ؓ, meant by this the qunut in the Fajr prayer.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا الصَّلْتُ بْنُ بَهْرَامَ ⦗ص: 591⦘ ، عَنْ أَبِي الشَّعْثَاءِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ «أَحَقُّ مَا بَلَغَنَا عَنْ إِمَامِكُمْ أَنَّهُ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَلَا يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَلَا يَرْكَعُ» ⦗ص: 593⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: يَعْنِي بِذَلِكَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما الْقُنُوتَ فِي صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, from Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, ؓ, that she used to lead women in prayer during the month of Ramadan, standing in the middle. Muhammad said: We do not approve of a woman leading the prayer, but if she does, she should stand in the middle of the row with the women, as Aisha, ؓ, did. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding the woman who sits in prayer. He said: "She may sit however she wishes." Muhammad said: It is more preferable to us that she gathers her legs to one side and does not sit upright like a man.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding the slave woman, who said: "She prays without a veil or head-covering, even if she reaches one hundred years of age, and even if she bears a child from her master."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, used to beat the slave women if they veiled themselves, saying: "Do not imitate the free women." Muhammad said: We adopt this position. We do not consider a slave woman to wear a veil, whether in prayer or otherwise, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding a woman who is in prayer and needs to alert someone. The answer is that she should clap. Muhammad said: However, it is more preferable to us that she refrains from doing so.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: The sun eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, on the day Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon them both, died. The people said, "The sun has eclipsed due to the death of Ibrahim." When this reached the Prophet, ﷺ, he addressed the people and said: "The sun and the moon are two of God’s signs; they do not eclipse due to the death or life of anyone." Then he prayed two rak'ahs, and supplication continued until the eclipse cleared. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and we do not see except one bowing in each rak'ah and two prostrations, unlike the people's prayer in other cases. We hold that they should pray in congregation during a solar eclipse, and only the imam who leads them in Friday prayer should lead the congregation. As for people praying in their mosques, that is not the case. Regarding reciting aloud, it has not reached us that the Prophet, ﷺ, recited aloud in it, but it has reached us that Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, recited aloud during it in Kufah. It is more preferable to us that recitation not be aloud in it. As for a lunar eclipse, people should pray individually, not in congregation, neither the imam nor others. The same applies to all frightening events. If the sun eclipses at a time when prayer is not permitted—such as at sunrise, midday, or after Asr—then there is no prayer at that time, but supplication continues until the eclipse clears or the time for prayer becomes permissible, and then they pray, even if some of the eclipse remains.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ انْكَسَفَتِ ⦗ص: 621⦘ الشَّمْسُ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَ مَاتَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا وَسَلَّمَ، فَقَالَ النَّاسُ: انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ لِمَوْتِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَخَطَبَ النَّاسَ فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ آيَتَانِ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَا يَنْكَسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلَا لِحَيَاتِهِ» ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ كَانَ الدُّعَاءُ حَتَّى انْجَلَتْ " ⦗ص: 630⦘ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَلَا نَرَى إِلَّا رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ، وَسَجْدَتَيْنِ عَلَى صَلَاةِ النَّاسِ فِي غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ، وَنَرَى أَنْ يُصَلُّوا جَمَاعَةً فِي كُسُوفِ الشَّمْسِ، وَلَا يُصَلِّي جَمَاعَةً إِلَّا الْإِمَامُ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي بِهِمُ الْجُمُعَةَ، فَأَمَّا أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ النَّاسُ فِي مَسَاجِدِهِمْ فَلَا، وَأَمَّا الْجَهْرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ، فَلَمْ يَبْلُغْنَا أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَهَرَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيهَا، وَبَلَغَنَا أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رضي الله عنه جَهَرَ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ ⦗ص: 632⦘ بِالْكُوفَةِ، وَأَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا أَنْ لَا يُجْهَرَ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ، وَأَمَّا كُسُوفُ الْقَمَرِ فَإِنَّمَا يُصَلِّي النَّاسُ وُحْدَانًا، وَلَا يُصَلُّونَ جَمَاعَةً، لَا الْإِمَامُ وَلَا غَيْرُهُ وَكَذَلِكَ الْأَفْزَاعُ كُلُّهَا، وَإِذَا انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ فِي سَاعَةٍ لَا يُصَلَّى فِيهَا عِنْدَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ ⦗ص: 634⦘ ، أَوْ نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ، أَوْ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ، فَلَا صَلَاةَ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ، وَلَكِنِ الدُّعَاءُ حَتَّى تَنْجَلِيَ أَوْ تَحِلَّ الصَّلَاةُ فَيُصَلِّي، وَقَدْ بَقِيَ مِنَ الْكُسُوفِ شَيْءٌ

records.raw_text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: The sun eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, on the day Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon them both, died. The people said, "The sun has eclipsed due to the death of Ibrahim." When this reached the Prophet, ﷺ, he addressed the people and said: "The sun and the moon are two of God’s signs; they do not eclipse due to the death or life of anyone." Then he prayed two rak'ahs, and supplication continued until the eclipse cleared. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and we do not see except one bowing in each rak'ah and two prostrations, unlike the people's prayer in other cases. We hold that they should pray in congregation during a solar eclipse, and only the imam who leads them in Friday prayer should lead the congregation. As for people praying in their mosques, that is not the case. Regarding reciting aloud, it has not reached us that the Prophet, ﷺ, recited aloud in it, but it has reached us that Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, recited aloud during it in Kufah. It is more preferable to us that recitation not be aloud in it. As for a lunar eclipse, people should pray individually, not in congregation, neither the imam nor others. The same applies to all frightening events. If the sun eclipses at a time when prayer is not permitted—such as at sunrise, midday, or after Asr—then there is no prayer at that time, but supplication continues until the eclipse clears or the time for prayer becomes permissible, and then they pray, even if some of the eclipse remains.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Asim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, who said: I asked him about musk being placed in the embalming mixture of the deceased. He said: Is it not among the finest of your perfumes? Muhammad said: And we adopt this position.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, ؓ, saw a deceased person whose head was being combed. She said: "Why do you adorn your deceased?" Muhammad said: We adopt this view—we do not see that the deceased’s head should be combed, nor should his hair be trimmed, nor his nails clipped. This is also the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a woman who dies among men, he said: "Her husband washes her, and likewise if a man dies among women, his wife washes him." Muhammad said: We adopt the view of Abu Hanifah, for a man has no waiting period; how can he wash his wife when it is lawful for him to marry her sister? And to marry her daughter if he has not consummated the marriage with her mother?

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding washing after washing the deceased. He said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, used to say, "If your companion was impure, then wash yourselves from him, but ablution suffices." Muhammad said: And if one wishes, he may also not perform ablution. If any of the water used to wash the deceased touches him, he should wash it off. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, used to order bathing after washing the deceased. Muhammad said: We do not see that he ordered it; rather, he considered it obligatory.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who is present at a funeral while he is not in a state of ablution. He said: "He should perform tayammum with clean earth and then pray, but a menstruating woman should not do that." Muhammad said: We adhere to this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad from Abu Hanifah who said Mansur ibn Mu'tamir narrated to us from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd from Ubayd ibn Nistas from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: "It is from the Sunnah to carry the funeral bier by its four sides. Whatever you add beyond that is a voluntary act." Muhammad said: We adopt this practice. A man begins by placing the deceased's front right side on his right, then places the deceased's back right side on his right. Then he moves to the front left and places it on his left, then comes to the back left and places it on his left. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: There is no recitation in funeral prayers, nor bowing, nor prostration. Instead, one gives salutations to the right and to the left when finished with the takbirs. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «لَا قِرَاءَةَ عَلَى الْجَنَائِزِ، وَلَا رُكُوعَ وَلَا سُجُودَ، وَلَكِنْ يُسَلِّمُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَعَنْ شِمَالِهِ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ التَّكْبِيرِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ ⦗ص: 68⦘ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: There is no fixed limit in the funeral prayer, but you begin by praising God, invoking blessings upon the Prophet, ﷺ, and supplicating to God for yourself and for the deceased as you wish.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim that he said regarding the prayer over the deceased: "The imams of the mosques should pray over them." It is appropriate for the guardian to present the imam of the mosque, but he is not compelled to do so. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that people used to pray over the deceased with five, six, or four takbirs until the Prophet, ﷺ, passed away. Then, after that, during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, ؓ, they continued to do so until Abu Bakr passed away. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, assumed leadership, and they continued the same practice during his caliphate. When Umar ibn al-Khattab saw this, he said: "O assembly of the Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, whenever you differ, those after you will differ as well. The people have only recently emerged from the Age of Ignorance. So agree upon something that those after you can unite upon." The opinion of the Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, then converged on examining the last funeral prayer the Prophet, ﷺ, had performed before his death, so they could adopt it and abandon all other practices. They investigated and found that the last funeral prayer the Messenger of God, ﷺ, had performed was with four takbirs. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى الْجَنَائِزِ خَمْسًا وَسِتًّا وَأَرْبَعًا، حَتَّى قُبِضَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثُمَّ كَبَّرُوا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي وِلَايَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه، حَتَّى قُبِضَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه، ثُمَّ وَلِيَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، فَفَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ فِي وِلَايَتِهِ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّاب رضي الله عنه، قَالَ «إِنَّكُمْ مَعْشَرَ أَصْحَابِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَتَى مَا تَخْتَلِفُونَ يَخْتَلِفُ مَنْ بَعْدَكُمْ، وَالنَّاسُ حَدِيثُ عَهْدٍ بِالْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَأَجْمِعُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ يَجْتَمِعُ عَلَيْهِ مَنْ بَعْدَكُمْ، فَأَجْمَعَ رَأْيُ أَصْحَابِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يَنْظُرُوا آخِرَ جَنَازَةٍ كَبَّرَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ قُبِضَ، فَيَأْخُذُونَ بِهِ فَيَرْفُضُونَ بِهِ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ، فَنَظَرُوا فَوَجَدُوا آخِرَ جَنَازَةٍ كَبَّرَ عَلَيْهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَرْبَعًا» قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
records.isnad_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim,
records.matn_en: that people used to pray over the deceased with five, six, or four takbirs until the Prophet, ﷺ, passed away. Then, after that, during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, ؓ, they continued to do so until Abu Bakr passed away. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, assumed leadership, and they continued the same practice during his caliphate. When Umar ibn al-Khattab saw this, he said: "O assembly of the Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, whenever you differ, those after you will differ as well. The people have only recently emerged from the Age of Ignorance. So agree upon something that those after you can unite upon." The opinion of the Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, then converged on examining the last funeral prayer the Prophet, ﷺ, had performed before his death, so they could adopt it and abandon all other practices. They investigated and found that the last funeral prayer the Messenger of God, ﷺ, had performed was with four takbirs. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim recounts Umar and Companion consensus; adoption is matn.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Al-Haytham narrated to us, from Abu Yahya Umayr ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he prayed over Yazid ibn al-Mukaffaf and said four takbirs. This was the last time Ali, ؓ, said takbir over the deceased.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim, "From where is the deceased placed into the grave?" He said, "From the side facing the qiblah, from where the funeral prayer is offered over him." He said: Someone who saw the people of Medina in the early times told me that they would place their deceased into the grave from the side of the qiblah, and that the practice of dragging (the body) was something the people of Medina introduced afterward. Muhammad said: The deceased is placed from the side of the qiblah, and he is not dragged from the side of the feet. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: One may enter the grave with an even or odd number of people, as both are good. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding funerals when they gather. He said: "They are arranged in a row, some in front of others, or all of them are arranged together. The imam stands in the middle of them. If there are men and women, the men are placed closest to the imam, and the women are placed in front of them toward the qiblah, just as men stand closest to the imam in prayer while women stand behind them." Muhammad said: We adhere to this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from Amir al-Sha'bi, who said: Ibn Umar, ؓ, led the funeral prayer for Umm Kulthum, the daughter of Ali, ؓ, and Zayd ibn Umar, her son. He placed Umm Kulthum toward the qiblah and placed Zayd next to the imam. Muhammad said: We adopt this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

narrator_path.source_form: عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَوْهَبٍ

records.boundary_review_note: Uthman explicitly reports his observation of Abu Hurayrah; page marker removed.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Al-Haytham narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Amr, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he prayed over a woman who had given birth to a child through adultery, and both she and her child had died, so Ibn Umar prayed over her. Muhammad said: We adopt this position—no one from the people of the Qiblah is to be left without prayer over them—and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا الْهَيْثَمُ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ صَلَّى عَلَى امْرَأَةٍ وَلَدَتْ مِنَ الزِّنَا، مَاتَتْ هِيَ وَابْنُهَا، فَصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا ابْنُ عُمَرَ ⦗ص: 156⦘ ، قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ لَا يُتْرَكُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقِبْلَةِ إِلَّا يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad who said: I saw Ibrahim walking ahead of the funeral procession, yet keeping some distance from it without disappearing from sight. Muhammad said: We see no harm in walking ahead of the funeral procession if one remains close to it, but walking behind it is preferable. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim about walking in front of the funeral procession. He said: Walk wherever you wish, but it is disliked for the people to go ahead and sit by the grave while leaving the funeral procession behind. Muhammad said: We adhere to this, and it is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us from Ibrahim, who said: I used to sit with the companions of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud— ؓ—such as Alqamah, Al-Aswad, and others. When a funeral procession passed by them while they were sitting cross-legged, none of them would untie his legs. Muhammad said: We adopt this practice and do not see that one should stand for the funeral procession, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah— ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, who said: I asked Ibrahim, "When should the people sit?" He replied, "When the funeral bier is placed down from the shoulders of the men." And he said, "What do you think if they reach the grave and no pickaxe has been struck in it, would you remain standing until the grave is dug?" Muhammad said: When the funeral bier is placed on the ground, there is no harm in sitting, but it is disliked before that. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that al-Harith ibn Abi Rabi'ah — his mother, who was a Christian, died. He followed her funeral procession with a group of the Prophet's companions. Muhammad said: We see no harm in following her, except that he should step aside from the funeral procession. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Someone who saw the grave of the Prophet, ﷺ, and the graves of Abu Bakr and Umar, ؓ, informed me that they were raised mounds from the earth, with white clay fragments on them. Muhammad said: We adopt this practice—the grave should be raised as a mound and not made square—and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.raw_text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Someone who saw the grave of the Prophet, ﷺ, and the graves of Abu Bakr and Umar, ؓ, informed me that they were raised mounds from the earth, with white clay fragments on them. Muhammad said: We adopt this practice—the grave should be raised as a mound and not made square—and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said, "Raise the grave so that it is recognized as a grave and not trodden upon." Muhammad said: We adopt this view, and we do not see that anything should be added to what has come out of it. We disapprove of plastering it, coating it with clay, building a mosque near it, placing a marker on it, or writing on it. We disapprove of using bricks in its construction or placing them inside the grave. We see no harm in sprinkling water on it, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, used to say, "I would rather step on a burning coal than intentionally step on a grave." records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim and from Awn ibn Abdullah, from al-Sha'bi, that they both said: "The husband has more right to lead the funeral prayer for the deceased than the father."

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah reported to me from a man, from al-Hasan, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he said "The father has more right to lead the funeral prayer for the deceased than the husband." Muhammad said: "We follow this, and Abu Hanifah, may God ﷻ be pleased with him, also followed this."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the stillborn: If it cries out, it is prayed over and inherited from. If it does not cry out, it is not prayed over nor inherited from. Muhammad said: We adopt this position. The crying out means that it falls alive, and this is the statement of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a child who is born dead after its form is fully developed, saying: "It is not prevented from (entering) Paradise, it does not inherit, and no funeral prayer is offered for it." Muhammad said: We adopt this view, but it is to be washed, shrouded, and buried. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding the man who is martyred and dies in the very place where he was killed: "His boots and cap are removed, and he is shrouded in the clothes he was wearing." Muhammad said: We adopt this position. Also, all leather and weapons are removed, and they may add whatever shrouds they wish. He is not washed, but the funeral prayer is performed over him. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifah, ؓ.
records.text_ar: مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يُسْتَشْهَدُ فَيَمُوتُ مَكَانَهُ الَّذِي قُتِلَ فِيهِ قَالَ «يُنْزَعُ عَنْهُ خُفَّاهُ وَقَلَنْسُوَتُهُ، وَيُكَفَّنُ فِي ثِيَابِهِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ» ⦗ص: 255⦘ ، قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ: وَبِهِ نَأْخُذُ، وَيُنْزَعُ أَيْضًا كُلُّ جِلْدٍ وَسِلَاحٍ وَيَزِيدُونَ مَا أَحَبُّوا مِنَ الْأَكْفَانِ، وَلَا يُغَسَّلُ، وَلَكِنْ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Salim al-Aftas narrated to us, saying: "There is no prophet except that he flees from his people to the Kaaba to worship its Lord, and indeed around it are the graves of three hundred prophets."

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: 'Ata ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: The graves of Hud, Salih, and Shu'ayb are in the Sacred Mosque.

records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah reported to us, saying: Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah narrated to us from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, ؓ, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: The destruction of my nation will be by the sword and the plague. records.text_en: Muhammad said Abu Hanifah informed us, saying: Alqamah ibn Marthad narrated to us from Ibn Buraydah al-Aslami, from his father, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said: I forbade you from visiting graves, but now visit them, and do not say anything offensive. Permission has been granted to Muhammad to visit his mother’s grave.
